author: British Museum
title: British Museum collection record for Oc.5849

notes.text:
The collection already has the nonspecific handle `rapa-britanico` (“Rapa — Londres”), but its source gives no accession or distinguishing description. This catalogue entry cannot be matched to that handle, and several selected BM dance-paddles could fit it. The catalogue labels this combined field “Found/Acquired”; it is retained as source wording and is not treated as an independently established findspot. A separate “Production place” field is represented as made_at when present.

30 September 2026 identity review: ambiguous crosswalk to `rapa-britanico`; keep this catalogue source unlinked. The British Museum identifies Museum number Oc.5849 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Oc-5849), a carved dance-paddle (rapa), 170 × 19.50 × 2.20 cm, associated with Lt M J Harrison and HMS Topaze. The Christy slip describes it as very similar to Oc.5848 but longer and lighter, and records possible canoe-board material and stitch holes. The BM page says collected on HMS Topaze's 1869 visit, while its acquisition note dates Harrison's stay to 1868; the discrepancy remains unresolved. The BM authorities for Lt M J Harrison (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/term/BIOG124174) and HMS Topaze (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/term/BIOG244775) list this accession. The generic Arte row says only Rapa and Museo Britanico/Londres and cannot distinguish this from Oc.5848 or Oc,+.2598, Oc,+.2599 and Oc,+.2600. Resolution needs an image or primary description tied to that specific Arte row, or a historical accession crosswalk.
